summary: npm package ships opaque Go binary implementing a WebRTC-signaled remote bash PTY backdoor
details: sextant-cli-linux-amd64@0.0.1-rc16 ships only a 13MB stripped Go ELF at bin/sxt and a package.json with no main/bin/scripts, declaring os=linux/cpu=x64 and a license field repurposed to point at https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control. The binary embeds github.com/pion/webrtc, github.com/pion/ice, github.com/pion/dtls, github.com/pion/turn, github.com/creack/pty, and exec.Command with /bin/bash and $SHELL: WebRTC DataChannel messages received from the hardcoded signaling endpoint wss://relay.sextant.top are written into a spawned bash PTY, giving the remote party a full interactive shell on the host. The binary also embeds http://ip-api.com for external IP/geolocation fingerprinting and the strings 'claude_control' and 'sextant'. The package name mimics a platform-specific optional-dependency sub-package (esbuild-linux-amd64 shape) so a parent 'sextant-cli' package would pull this binary onto installer machines transitively.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
